correctness.rationale: For every N>=2, positive cyclic gaps, r,D>0, the explicit positive normalized periodic density satisfies the distributional forward equation with reset destination masses given by the two adjacent tanh half-gap factors. A piecewise-sinh lifted harmonic coordinate is C1 across every Voronoi boundary and harmonic for D d2/dx2+r(f(Q)-f); the associated martingale has bounded jumps, a bounded x-corrector, and bracket whose exact stationary integral evaluates to \(rL^2/(2ST)\). Ergodicity and the martingale CLT yield a zero-drift Gaussian limit and variance rate \(rL^2/(4ST)\). Taylor expansions prove the fixed-rate strict reversal; dominant exponentials prove high-rate bottleneck. The independent tilted reset-chain method agrees with the theorem in six profiles and 235 finite checks. Limitations: finite checks are not substitutes for the infinite analytic argument.

originality.rationale: The motivating open preprint and supplementary material treat the same model but analytically evaluate regular spacing, give a global rate-optimized bound, and establish a generic weak-reset enhancement. They do not evaluate the complete arbitrary-gap transport coefficient or its exact stationary reset-site law, fixed-rate disorder reversal, or largest-gap asymptotic. Uniform-array cumulant findings in accessible local records are not covering. Seven explicit published-record queries and targeted primary literature searches did not identify an equivalent or stronger evaluated theorem. This is qualified best-knowledge originality, not certified uniqueness.

value.rationale: The arbitrary-array transport coefficient is the central macroscopic observable left analytically unresolved in the motivating model, allowing exact evaluation for every positive gap vector without a coupled numerical stationary-site calculation. It yields a real design trade-off: nonuniform arrangements improve diffusivity at sufficiently weak fixed rates, even though optimized-rate regular spacing wins globally; at strong rates the single largest gap determines the exponential barrier. The explicit invariant spatial law and site-choice probabilities permit direct transport and spatial-distribution comparisons. These are motivated structural results beyond re-labeling the equal-gap formula.
